newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK second quarter C/A, GDP data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK second quarter C/A, GDP data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to data showing UK GDP grew 0.5 percent in the second quarter of 1996 from the previous quarter and was up 2.2 percent from second quarter 1995. The second quarter current account surplus was 457 million stg:
The Reuters consensus forecast for GDP was +0.4 percent quarter-on-quarter and +1.8 percent vs second quarter 1995. For the current account the forecast was for a 1.2 bln stg deficit.
"No dramatic surprises from the growth figures. The economy was still growing below trend in the second quarter."
The big suprise is the current account figures which were in healthy surplus and this should be another factor giving sterling some support...but these figures do not rule out another rate cut."

"The current account is clearly very good news, it's the largest surplus since 1987. Certainly no sign that any of the external demand weakness and domestic demand strength we've seen in the UK economy over the last six months or so is leading to any deterioration in the overseas financial position."
"Upward revisions to GDP tend to come in the expansion phase. Further evidence here that the UK economy is about to enjoy above trend GDP growth."

"These figures should lend some support to the pound and have led to a small upward revision to second quarter GDP which may also be helpful to the currency. The trade surplus is the first since the first quarter 1995 and the largest surplus since the first quarter 1987. The major improvements came in the service and investment sectors."
